title: Who's About to Crash the Pop Charts? Meet Three Rising Stars!
summary: The top of the pop charts might look the same this week—Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' is still number one for the 12th week! But if you peek just below the top 10, you'll spot three songs climbing fast, like sneaky ninjas about to crash the party. First up is Stella Lefty, a country-pop singer whose song 'Boston' jumped to number 13. It borrows a melody from Noah Kahan's hit 'Stick Season,' but adds a sunny, feel-good twist. It's the kind of song you'd blast with the car windows down on a summer day. Next, at number 19, is Yung Miami with 'Spend Dat.' She's been making music for years, both solo and as part of the duo City Girls, but this is her biggest hit ever—her first solo song to even reach the top 40! Finally, at number 22, is Malcolm Todd with 'Earrings.' He's been popular on TikTok, and his new album just debuted in the top five. 'Earrings' is his highest-charting song yet. Meanwhile, on the albums chart, K-pop group ATEEZ stormed to number one with their new EP Golden Hour: Part.5, selling 223,000 copies in its first week—thanks partly to 30 different CD versions! They knocked Olivia Rodrigo to second place. With summer heating up, these rising stars might just give Ella Langley a run for her money. Who knows? Maybe next week, one of them will be in the top 10!
why_it_matters: Just like you might discover a new favorite song while scrolling through TikTok, these artists show how quickly someone can go from unknown to famous—so keep listening, the next big hit could be from someone you've never heard of yet.

Article_Structure: WHO: Rising pop and country artists Stella Lefty, Yung Miami, Malcolm Todd, and K-pop group ATEEZ.
WHAT: Their songs are climbing the pop singles chart, and ATEEZ’s new EP debuted at number one on the albums chart.
WHERE: On the Billboard Hot 100 singles chart and the Billboard 200 albums chart in the U.S.
WHY: Thanks to catchy tunes, social media buzz on TikTok, and dedicated fan bases buying multiple album versions.
